## AETHELGARD // Ether-Core Extraction

A playable first-person extraction slice set in the badlands of Aethelgard. Cross the dunes,
crack supply caches, mine glowing Ether-Core, put down rogue drones, and hold Lift 04 long
enough to bank your haul. Die — or abandon the run — and the wasteland keeps the cargo.

This is a self-contained Three.js prototype with no build step and no runtime network calls.

### Run it

```bash
# from this directory, using any static file server
python3 -m http.server 3002
# then open http://localhost:3002
```

In the OMGithub playground, `./start.sh` serves the same static site.

### Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W` `A` `S` `D` | Move |
| `Shift` | Sprint (drains stamina) |
| `Space` | Jump |
| `Left mouse` | Fire (full-auto) |
| `Right mouse` | Aim down sights |
| `R` | Reload |
| `E` | Interact / mine / call lift |
| `Esc` | Pause |
| `Touch` | On-screen stick, fire, reload and use buttons |

### Economy note

The economy is **simulated for the prototype**. Extracted Scrap and $AETHER are written to a
local wallet in `localStorage` under `aethelgard.wallet.v1`; there is no wallet connection,
token, or blockchain transaction. One Ether-Core pays out 25 $AETHER on a successful ascent.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

{"body":"Core Pitch

• Genre: First-Person Open-World Looter-Shooter / Extraction & Survival RPG
• Platform: PC / mobile (Built on Solana or BNB Chain for micro-transactions)
• Monetization/Tokenomics: Dual-currency economy featuring an off-chain utility currency (Scrap) and an on-chain native utility token (AETHER) alongside Solana/BNB-backed NFTs for rare gear, land plots, and vehicles.

Setting & Narrative

• The World: A shattered, post-collapse mega-structure or terraformed desert planet called Aethelgard, where a rare energy-dense mineral known as Ether-Core crashed from orbit.
• The Premise: You play as a Free-Scrapper dropped into a massive, seamless 64km² open-world map. Rival factions, rogue AI drones, and hostile players fight over shifting Ether-storms. Extracting the glowing isotope lets you refine it into real-world tradable token value—or risk losing everything if you get gunned down before reaching an extraction elevator.

Gameplay Loop (First-Person Combat & Exploration)

1. Explore: Traverse the open wasteland via foot, modular cyber-buggies, or glider-wings. Weather events change the map layout and reveal rare mineral veins.
2. Engage: High-stakes FPS gunplay featuring ballistic recoil, customizable attachment crafting, and mid-match ability modification (swapping cybernetic limb modules on the fly, similar to Off the Grid).
3. Loot & Survive: Scavenge weapon parts, tactical armor, and raw Ether-Core. PvEvP zones mean you are battling both environmental hazards and real players.
4. Extract or Lose: Reach a secure bunker or call in a dropship. Successful extraction turns your physical loot into account points and $AETHER tokens. Dying in the red-zone strips your non-insured gear into the global pool for other players to grab.

Web3 & Crypto Integration

• Dual Currency System:
	• Scrap (In-Game Soft Currency): Earned by completing basic PvE quests, killing AI patrols, and crafting standard gear. Used for repairs and basic ammo.
	• $AETHER (On-Chain Token): Earned through high-tier extraction zones, weekly faction control wars, and ranked PvP tournaments. Can be traded on external DEXs, staked for passive governance power, or used to purchase cosmetic blueprints and safehouse land plots.
• NFT True Ownership:
	• Weapon Blueprints & Cyberware: Minted as tradable digital assets on the marketplace.
	• Sector Deeds (Land/Safehouses): Players can own a piece of the open world, collecting a small passive tax or storage fee when other players use their safehouse crafting stations.

Key Features for Development

• Seamless World: No loading screens between the hub city and the wild badlands.
• Dynamic Faction Wars: Weekly territory control dictates which player alliance controls the main refinery, altering the global drop rates for $AETHER.
• Anti-Cheat & Fair Play: Strict reputation systems and hardware checks to prevent botting or automated farming rings from ruining the open-world economy.
